Some drugs are used to inhibit intestinal enzymes, such as 
the diabetic drugs acarbose (Precose) and miglitol (Glyset), 
which are a-glucosidase inhibitors. These medications lead to a 
delayed and reduced rise in postprandial blood glucose levels 
and plasma insulin responses. The major adverse effect is GI 
intolerance, specifically diarrhea, flatulence, and cramping 
secondary to the osmotic effect and bacterial fermentation of 
undigested carbohydrates in the distal bowel.
